census2022.source: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, Population and Housing Census 2022 (final enumerated count)

verification.method: scripts/verify/bangladesh.py reads the original UN files directly (not the site's generated data) and compares them with the built page, JSON-LD, CSV and home page; then a hand read of title, description, headline, FAQ and story text.
what: Population 1960–2050 (all table years), world rank, share of world, growth rate, yearly change, people per day, density, land area, net migration, emigration peak and since-when, median age, births per woman, 2050 projections
Urban share 1960, 2026, 2050, urban people, first year above 50%
Dhaka North and South city corporation populations (2022 census) and their sum
Home page world population, yearly change and featured Bangladesh figure
Title, meta description, Article headline and citations, Dataset sources and licence, FAQ answers in JSON-LD
against: UN WPP 2024 original file WPP2024_Demographic_Indicators_Medium.csv.gz (SHA-256 286ac36b…, downloaded 2026-11-25) — 63 of 63 figures match
UN WUP 2025 original file WUP2025-F15-National-Definitions_percPop_by_category.xlsx (SHA-256 5fdc43a9…, downloaded 2026-11-25); licence CC BY 3.0 IGO stated in the file

BBS Population and Housing Census 2022 final figures for Dhaka North (5,990,723) and Dhaka South (4,305,063), as reported by citypopulation.de (citing BBS) and The Financial Express; BBS original PDF not opened
verification.result: All figures match. No image alt text on the page (charts carry aria-labels).

changelog.change: Yearly growth corrected to 1.2% and 2,123,011 people a year (shown before as 1.21% and 2,131,144), and people added per day to 5,816 (was 5,839). The year net emigration peaked corrected to 2008 (was given as about 2010). The urban share is now credited to its real source, UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025 (it was credited to World Population Prospects 2024; the figures did not change). Four statements without a source were removed (a comparison with US states, a claim about other countries taking a century, the main destinations of workers abroad, and an "unusually large" working-age share).
All UN figures are now read directly from the original UN files and re-checked.
